subject: contract-snapshot-envelope
text:
**Snapshot envelope** (atomically replaced JSON)
```json
{"v":1,"written_at":"2026-09-23T19:43:58.123Z","writer":"0.1.0","data":{}}
```
A snapshot whose `v` is higher than the reader supports, or that fails to parse, is ignored, and the state is rebuilt by replaying `events.ndjson`. Replay recovers only log-derived fields: `links`, `agent_session_id`, `wheel`, `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until`. Fields no event carries (`endpoint`, `pid`, `started_at`, `pinned_bin`, `statusline_command`, `cli_version`, `cli_verified`, `child_pid`, `pending_dialog`, `cwd`) are treated as absent. Liveness then rests on the heartbeat alone, so the instance is `live` or gone and never `stale`. The endpoint is rebuilt as described under IPC endpoints, and `hook statusline` prints nothing. As landed the fallback is library code in `viola-state` with six product readers, each after the instance's strict-modes check has passed: `viola revive`'s preflight takes it in its second reading, the logged session (chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive; second of four since chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board added `session-live`, the strict-modes check ahead of the preflight since chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor), and `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::read` (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list), which gives a `list` payload item for a replayed snapshot only when the beat is at most `STALE_AFTER` (5 s) old: `live`, never `stale`, `dialog_pending: false`, no CLI field, `wheel` / `budget_paused` only where the log gave one; an absent snapshot or a failed replay gives no item. The other four are `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (Session liveness, below); `viola hook`'s `connect`, which reads a replayed or absent snapshot as unreachable, so the hook fails open; `hook statusline`'s `serve`, which finds no `statusline_command` in a replayed snapshot; and `run`'s collision check, which takes its caller's one read and judges a replayed snapshot by the heartbeat alone (`already-live` when the beat is at most `STALE_AFTER` old, else free; an absent snapshot or a failed read is free). `viola revive`'s preflight hands its one read to both its collision check and its recorded-directory reading. `snapshot::read_snapshot_classified` tells four cases apart through the same `MAX_FRAME` bound: the snapshot, no file, an unreadable one, and an unsupported one with the `v` it saw. It reads the envelope's `v` first: above 1 is unsupported whatever else the envelope holds, 1 must then parse whole, and anything else (a `v` of 0 included) is unreadable.
 `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` replays the log for an unreadable or unsupported snapshot, in one pass, and logs one `state-recovered` line; an absent snapshot is neither replayed nor logged, and the replay writes no file. It recovers `wheel` and the budget gate from their last line and `agent_session_id` from the last `session-start` that carries one; a field no line gave is absent, never a default; `links` is recovered in the same pass through the public rule `viola_state::replay::apply_link_line` (chunk 2026-10-10-session-links): a `link` line whose `data.driver` and `data.driven` are strings adds `{driver, driven, since}` with `since` that line's `ts` unless the set holds the pair, an `unlink` line removes the pair, and a line of another kind or with a name that is no string changes nothing. A `link` line with no string `ts` gets `since: "unknown"`, the form `session_chain` takes for a missing `ts`; no writer of this build makes such a line, and the shape stands on the operator's word, the founder not having ruled on it. `read_snapshot` keeps its results and has no product caller (the rule: `read_snapshot(` under `src/`, outside test modules, as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity/report.md`). A replayed snapshot gives no `cwd`, so a revive over one is refused `cwd-missing`. Beside the replay, `replay::session_chain` reads the logged sessions for revive in one pass over `events.ndjson` through `events::read_from`: one link per `session-start` line whose `agent_session_id` is a string, with the pass's skip counts. It writes and logs nothing.

subject: contract-channel-methods
text: - `list` is not a channel method. The calling process reads `instances/*/` (heartbeat and snapshot) and `claude agents --json` itself, so `list` needs no live wrapper. Its `ok` payload (CLI `--json` and MCP `list`) is `{items, budget, skipped}`, with the item, `budget` and `skipped` shapes of the `list` payload above. As landed (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list), CLI `list` reads `<home>/instances/` (`viola_state::board::scan`, then `board::read`) and `budget.json` (through `read_budget_stamped`) and contacts no wrapper. Since chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board it then makes one `claude agents --json` read (`run::agents::read_here`, `claude` resolved by `run::resolve_program` from its current directory) and joins it by `viola_state::board::join`: a row matching a wrapped item's `child_pid` or `agent_session_id` sets that item's `status` to `idle` or `busy`; every unjoined row is an unwrapped item (`wrapped: false`, its name the row's `sessionId`, `live`, `dialog_pending: false`, no `wheel` / `budget_paused` / `cli_version` / `cli_verified`), sorted by name after the wrapped items. A failed, oversize or malformed read leaves the board as `board::read` gave it (every `status` `unknown`, no unwrapped item). The join field is ledger row `agents-join`. MCP `list` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) builds the same board through `list::board_document` (scan → read → document, the provider `viola mcp` hands `viola_mcp::serve`) and returns the document's `ok`, or `instance-unreachable` for the board's refusal; CLI `list` keeps its own order (scan, its log opened, read, document).

subject: contract-cli-json-output
text: - `viola link <driver> <driven> --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"since":…,"already_linked":…}}` (`since` a string, `already_linked` a boolean) and `viola unlink <driver> <driven> --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{}}`, each with exit 0. Their refused strict-modes check on the home and `instances/<driven>`, made before any role file or log opens, prints exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` on stdout (exit 21), with stderr empty and no line in any log.

subject: contract-cli-json-output
text: - `viola send`, `viola wait`, `viola last`, `viola answer`, `viola pause` and `viola release` print the same `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` on stdout under `--json` (exit 21) for their refused strict-modes check of the home and the target instance, made by `client::refuse_untrusted` before anything under the home is opened, with stderr empty and no line in any log.

subject: contract-session-liveness
text: - The server identity read is `viola_state::liveness`'s. `live_endpoint(instance_dir)` returns `Option<LiveEndpoint>`, `LiveEndpoint { endpoint, pid, started_at }`, all from its one `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` call and only on a real snapshot (a replayed or absent one, or a failed read, gives `None`), so a frame-writing client takes the instance's strict-modes check first, then the liveness-only pre-check, then the server check. The closed decision enum `ServerVerdict` (no crate error enum) is `Matches` · `Mismatch` · `Unverifiable`. The pure `server_verdict(recorded_pid, started_at, observed_pid, observed_start, peer_pid_reported)` compares the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` (whole seconds, read through its RFC 3339 form) with the observed peer pid and that process's OS start time; with `peer_pid_reported` false, as on macOS, which reports no peer pid, it returns `Matches` with no comparison: the recorded gap. The joined `verify_server(recorded_pid, started_at, observed_pid, peer_pid_reported)` reads the observed start time through `process_start_time` (a zombie reads none) and returns `server_verdict`'s verdict.

subject: res-binaries
text:
- Subcommands: `run`, `revive`, `send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `hook <event>`, `mcp`, `verify`, `pause`, `release` (incl. `--budget`), `link`, `unlink`, `plugin install`. `mcp` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) is hidden from `viola --help` (`#[command(hide = true)]`: run by the plugin, never by a person) and takes no argument but the global `--home`; it serves the five tools over stdio until stdin closes or a stdin line passes `MAX_FRAME`, which ends the session as a close does (exit 0 once initialized, 1 before `initialize`, both streams empty), and exits 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr and no role file when its home or `diagnostics/` (each that exists) fails `viola_state::strict::check_path`.
 `verify` takes `[--record <DIR>] [-- <program> [args…]]` (program default `claude`). `list` takes `[--json]` and nothing else; it exits 0 with a board (one stdout write), 21 when its strict-modes check refuses the home, `instances/` or any one instance (the whole board refused), 1 for an internal error through the `cli` catch site and 2 for a clap usage error (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list). `plugin install` takes `[--json]` and nothing else (`viola plugin` alone is a clap usage error; clap's own `viola plugin help` is served); it exits 0 with its result (one stdout write), 21 when its strict-modes check refuses the home or any existing `marketplace/` tree dir (nothing created, no log opened), 1 for an internal error through the `cli` catch site and 2 for a clap usage error. `revive` takes `<name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [-- <child args>]`, or `<name> --list`, each with `[--json]`; under `--json` a refused strict-modes check or a preflight refusal is the exit-1 `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document (one of the five codes, §Standard Contracts) with stderr empty, and `--list --json` prints the `ok.sessions` document, or the `no-session` document with exit 1; it exits 0 when the revived child's wrapper ends as `run`'s does, 1 for a refused strict-modes check or a preflight refusal and 2 for a clap usage error (a malformed `--id` included).

subject: res-binaries
text: - `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` exit 21 when their instance check refuses, as `link` / `unlink` do (human: the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr; `--json`: the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` document on stdout). `verify` exits 1 with the home-state pair, before its `cli` log and any step line, when `check_home_tree` refuses its home, `ledger/`, `bin/` or `plugin/`, or `update_stamps` refuses `ledger/stamps.json`. `run` and `revive`'s start exit 1 before any log when the home-tree check refuses (`revive --json` keeps its `strict-modes-failed` document). How a home under a regular file reads on each OS: Filesystem, `instances/<ViolaName>/`, below.

subject: res-filesystem
res-filesystem
text:
- `instances/<ViolaName>/events.ndjson`, `events.ndjson.lock`, `snapshot.json`, `snapshot.json.lock`, `heartbeat`, `settings.json` (the per-session settings override that wraps the statusline; Unix only, see Claude Code integration names), `diagnostics/` (the owner-only content-bearing detail files `detail-<role>.ndjson`, such as the panic payload and backtrace in `detail-run.ndjson`; dir 0700, files 0600 on Unix; one `write` per line; file format owned by obs and fixed by `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json`. Codes-only process lines go to the home-level role files). v1 never rotates or truncates `events.ndjson`, because `wait`'s `after` and `send`'s `cursor` are byte offsets into it. Bounding its size is an open item, and any scheme must keep existing offsets valid. These entry points check these files before they use them: `viola list`; `viola revive`; `viola run`'s start (through `check_home_tree` with its name); `viola hook`'s statusline, event and dialog paths (sharing `trusted`); `viola mcp`'s frame tools; and the CLI frame verbs `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` (sharing `client::refuse_untrusted`). `viola list` (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `viola_state::board::scan` runs `check_path` on the home and on `instances/`, each that exists (absent passes, an unstattable one is refused), reads each entry's type without following a link (a link, a non-directory or a name that is no `ViolaName` gives no instance and is only counted), joins a path only from a parsed name, then runs `check_instance` per instance in name order, all before any file under the home is opened and before its log starts; the first failure refuses the whole board with exit 21 (`--json`: `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` on stdout, stderr empty; human: the instance-state or the home-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr, stdout empty), no log opened, no line written and the home's mode left as found — the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13).
 `viola revive` (the start arm and `--list`) runs `viola_state::strict::check_instance` over the home (the read rule), `instances/` (the write rule), the instance directory (the read rule), its `diagnostics/` (the read rule), its `snapshot.json` (the write rule) and its `events.ndjson` (the write rule on Unix, the read rule on Windows), each that exists and a folder before what it holds, before its wrapper log opens, and a refusal is exit 1 with the state-files `unable:` / `hint:` pair (under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"strict-modes-failed","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty): no log opened, no line written (no `process-start`, no `process-exit`), no child started and the home's mode left as found. `viola hook statusline` runs the same check on its canonicalised instance directory before anything under the home is read or opened; a refused instance returns exit 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file opened, no `hook-invoked` or `hook-decision` line, no stdin read, no command run, nothing printed and `budget.json` untouched. Neither arm writes the word `strict-modes-failed` on any line. `viola link` / `viola unlink` run `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<driven>` before `client::start`, so before any role file or log opens and before any snapshot value is read; a refusal is exit 21 (`--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}` document on stdout, stderr empty; human the instance-state `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr), no line written and the mode left as found. Each of these checks comes first because opening a log sets an existing home to 0700 (as measured on the statusline arm at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through, `evidence/red-green.md` §3), and a check made after it passes a home at 0770. Both orders were fixed at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor: before it `revive`'s start arm opened its log first, and a home at 0770 came back 0700 and passed the check (as measured at that chunk's `research.md`, runs C and D, and `evidence/red-green.md` (a)), and the statusline arm opened its log after a refused check, so its refusal lasted one invocation (`evidence/red-green.md` (b)). That a refused check leaves no trace on the statusline arm is the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at that chunk's planning, superseded 2026-10-13). `check_instance` has these three product call sites (`src/cmd/hook.rs` `trusted`, shared by the statusline, event and dialog paths; `src/cmd/revive.rs`; and `src/cmd/client.rs` `refuse_untrusted`, shared by `link` / `unlink` and the six frame verbs; the rule: `check_instance(` under `src/`). Outside that rule `viola-mcp`'s `tools.rs` `frame` calls it, and `run`'s start reaches its set through `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree`.
 The check is proven on Unix (five widened modes). On Windows `cfg(windows)` cases prove it: an instance tree granted Users write is refused `Writable` beside a `create_private_dir` tree that passes, a `diagnostics/` granted Users read is refused, and a plain home made before viola is refused for its inherited write grant to a SID `trusted_sid` does not trust, read by its right whichever SID holds it, while a home `instance_tree()` makes reads none (as measured at ci#40439188053, `windows-2025`).

subject: res-filesystem
text: - The other checked entry points run the instance check first, each refusing with nothing under the home opened, no line written and the mode or ACL left as found: the CLI frame verbs `send` (after its text read), `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` through `client::refuse_untrusted`, which `link` / `unlink` share, before any snapshot value is read (their exits: Binaries, above); `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths through `trusted`, before `read_diagnostics_level` and obs init, with its two `--capture` arms ahead of it (exit 0, with no `config.json` read, role file, stdin read, frame or SessionEnd append); `viola mcp`'s frame tools before `live_endpoint` (`instance-unreachable` with `detail: null`, no frame); and `viola run`'s and `viola revive`'s starts through `check_home_tree` before `open_wrapper_log` (the home pair, or the instance pair for an instance-level refusal, and no child).

subject: res-filesystem
text: - A path under a regular file stats `NotFound` on Windows, so the strict-modes check skips it as absent and the `cli` catch-site line stands there; on Unix the same home is a strict-modes refusal (`verify` exits 1 with the home pair, the frame verbs exit 21 with the instance pair). A test that plants a regular file above a checked path therefore needs a per-OS oracle (as measured at ci#40398601594, `windows-2025`).

subject: res-filesystem
text: - Test-only, outside the viola home: `<temp dir>/viola-root-watch/<test name, :: → .>.<label>.report` — the root test support `tests/support/watch.rs` `Watch` (bound `WITHIN` = 7 s, shared by the root waits on a child: `Instant::now() + WITHIN` reads 28 sites in 20 files under `tests/`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor's wrap on the Linux dev host's final tree (two more than at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive: one each in `tests/cli_budget.rs`, a new file, and `tests/cli_revive.rs`), the shared `tests/support/events.rs` and `tests/support/cli.rs` holding one each; that pattern is the count's rule and not a census of every wait on the bound. One of the waits is `tests/support/home.rs` `wait_endpoint_gone`, which `Wrapper::stop` / `stop_keep` run after the wrapper's exit until the snapshot's recorded `endpoint` is unconnectable; after a kill, `Wrapper::kill` waits on `holder_gone` instead (on Unix a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent, on Windows the pipe is not found), because a killed wrapper removes nothing and its socket file stays on Unix, where the stop path's rule is the file being absent (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, the kill-and-revive case green on the three CI runners)). It is created empty at the wait's start and gets a line only when the polled state changes (codes, counts and booleans only), so a test the runner kills keeps its evidence. It is kept when the test panics or is killed and removed when it passes. `viola` never reads or writes it.

subject: crosscut-config
text:
- **Config management.** Precedence: CLI flags override `<viola home>/config.json`, which overrides built-in defaults.
  - Viola home: a global `--home <dir>` flag on every subcommand overrides the default `<user home>/.viola/`. Resolution order: `--home`, then the grandparent of `VIOLA_DIR` when it is set, then the default. As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): `resolve_home(flag, name, dir, user_home)` in `src/cmd/mod.rs` resolves `--home` as given, else the `instance_of` home when both `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` pass the one shape check (a valid `ViolaName`, an absolute dir ending `instances/<name>`), else `<user home>/.viola`, a failing pair falling through; `resolved_home` reads the two variables and `std::env::home_dir()` once, at every verb arm of `dispatch`; `canonical_home` canonicalises a home that exists (`std::fs::canonicalize`, a Windows `\\?\C:\…` written back as `C:\…`, every other verbatim form kept) and keeps `std::path::absolute`'s spelling for one that does not, creating nothing; `run`'s start canonicalises the home after its wrapper log has created it, before the collision check, the pin and the endpoint bind. `viola run --home <dir>` passes the home to the child only through `VIOLA_DIR`, so the pinned copy, plugin folder, endpoint hash, logs, `budget.json` and ledger stamps all follow it. The statusline source follows the home too: `<home>/statusline-source.json` is the source whenever it exists, and only the default home (`canonical_home(default_home(user_home))`, `default_home` shared by `resolve_home` and the source rule) falls back to the user's `<user home>/.claude/settings.json`, so a home named by `--home` or reached through `VIOLA_DIR` never reads the user's settings. The rule has no `config.json` key and no environment variable; `start` reads `std::env::home_dir()` for it, the read `resolved_home` already made. This is the isolation point for tests: each test runs in its own home, and that home's `ledger/stamps.json` can stamp the fake agent's reported version.
  - `viola hook` takes the `instance_of` session only when its `VIOLA_DIR` instance directory exists (`canonical`) and passes `check_instance` (`trusted`; both in `src/cmd/hook.rs`, shared by the event, dialog and statusline arms), before `diagnostics_level` is read from `config.json` or obs starts: a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing instance directory, or an instance the check refuses, makes the hook exit 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd append. The two `--capture` arms, which read no `VIOLA_*`, stay ahead of it.
  - `config.json` is parsed tolerantly (unknown keys skipped and counted) and carries `v`.
  - Settings: budget thresholds as `Percent` (defaults `five_hour` 90, `seven_day` 85), `diagnostics_level` (`info` by default, or `debug`) and `claude_env_keep` (the Unix R8 pass-list of `CLAUDE*` names, default empty) and `dialog_hold_s` (the dialog hold as a `DialogHold`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60). `diagnostics_level` is the only source of the process-log level; `RUST_LOG` has no effect.
  - There are no secrets in v1, and environment variables are not a configuration channel. The `VIOLA_*` variables are wrapper-to-child plumbing set by `viola run` only. The only other variables any `viola` build reads are the two test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (capped at 5 s) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (exact value `1`, a forced fail-open `hook` panic), both compiled only under `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")` and absent from release builds, and, in every build, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM`, read by viola's own colour layer (`src/human/style.rs`, `viola list`'s human mode only) to decide whether and how deep its SGR bytes are written (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline): they configure nothing, disable no control and widen no redaction. viola's reader is the only one because clap is built without its `color` feature: that feature's anstream → anstyle-query route read `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `COLORTERM` and `CI` and was closed at chunk 2026-09-28-cli-output-tokens (as measured at its research F1: `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 viola --help` into a pipe gave 25 ESC bytes before, 0 after); a dependency or feature that reads an environment variable breaks this rule like a direct read does.

subject: crosscut-sanitised-error-surfaces
text:
- **Sanitised error surfaces.** CLI `--json` documents, MCP error results and channel error data carry codes and fixed messages only, no path and no upstream text; a peer's `message`, `data`, `refusal` or `detail` reaches no document or text but as a closed value, and a code word outside the closed list stays visible by design.
  - The E2E contract binary `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` (run under `run --e2e`, carrying `andromeda:walks-tree`) holds it: its tables `CLI_DOCUMENTS`, `MCP_RESULTS` and `CHANNEL_FAULTS` enumerate the error bodies, and `error_bodies_each_name_a_writer_and_a_witness_that_stand` checks that each body's writer and witness stand; `NOT_ERROR_BODIES` names what is no error body, and `PLUMBING` the census lines that build or route a document a row names, so a row stays one body. A census, `product_error_writers_are_each_named`, covers the product's error writers, and `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing` holds that a `thiserror` message interpolates nothing.
  - Three surface witnesses read the bodies: `cli_error_documents_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` in `tests/cli_error_bodies.rs`, `channel_error_bodies_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` in `tests/channel_error_bodies.rs` and `mcp_tools_error_results_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text` in `crates/viola-e2e/tests/mcp_tools.rs`. The two root binaries' `[[test]]` tables require the `fake-agent` feature, and both sit in the `ci` profile's kill-line filter.
  - No `-32603` is driven in a scanned home, and no failpoint or counted panic exists for it: the unit layer holds it, through `answer_a_panicking_dispatch_is_internal_error_and_closes` and `links_set_method_an_append_that_fails_is_internal_with_the_set_unchanged`.
